standards: Michigan Personal Finance foundations — introductory
Grade 3 economics and mathematics connections
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 3
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G3 Unit 1 — needs, wants, and choosing

prompts.prompt: Explain what a need is in your own words and give or identify one valid example.
Use a drawing, chart, checklist, demonstration, or worked process to show understanding of what a want is.
Apply why we cannot have everything in a new realistic situation. Show the steps or give the evidence.
Analyze a plausible mistake, faulty assumption, or weak claim involving naming what we gave up; correct it and explain why the correction is better.
Connect what a need is with steps of a careful choice. Explain how the two ideas support or depend on one another.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit project: Build a pretend choice board that compares two make-believe options and names the tradeoff for each one.
Name one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application and adequate evidence or reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the smallest gap and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source, not the sole basis for long-term mastery.
